title: C567 — Driver door side impact sensor connector
introduction:
I use this reference as an address book for the driver-door sensor wiring: the connector outline identifies the housing, and the cavity labels lead to the individual circuit records. Start with the identity table, then use the drawing and pin table together. Keep the housing Color entry separate from the wire Color entries.

This guide covers identification and reading the reference. The drawing's physical viewing side is unlabelled, so its page orientation is not a probing instruction. Access, electrical testing, wire selection and replacement require separate procedures. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes remain undefined here.

edits.why: I use the upper latch outline and the unequal side projections to recognize the drawing's orientation on the page. The cavities sit side by side. Their printed labels connect the illustration to the Cavity column; the table beneath the drawing associates this view with its shell and harness record.

Find a cavity label in the drawing, locate its row, then read across for the circuit identifier, wire color, gauge, function and terminal reference. The sensor and control-module wording describes the listed circuit roles; it is not a basis for assigning power, ground or polarity. A matching record identifies a connection, without proving its electrical condition.

The kit Number leads across to its Service Part and Engineering Shell entries. These describe the listed service assembly, while Terminal Part Number in the pin table refers to the cavity contact. Keep the circuit-wire and pigtail Gauge entries attached to their own rows. The shared shell listing does not supply a rule for choosing between the kits.
